newTerms.Spirit of the Truth of a universe: Espíritu de la Verdad de un universo

forcedChoices.choice: tú for the first two sentences (to Thomas), ustedes from «Ustedes, que conocen a Dios»
forcedChoices.reason: Jesus names Thomas first; the English moves to a plural address with 'You who are God-knowing'.

forcedChoices.choice: servants say «usted» to the lord; the lord says «tú» to the servants
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish rule: usted for great respect to a ruler; a master speaks to a servant with tú.
Plain adjective here, not the term 'actual' (en acto) of 0:4.7.

forcedChoices.choice: the exclamation 'What a sorry sight ... to say ...' ends with «!» after the quote
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish needs ¡…! around the whole exclamation; the inner quote stays at the same place.

forcedChoices.choice: 'The things which you now look down upon' as «Las cosas que ahora ven desde aquí arriba»
forcedChoices.reason: Context (on the mount, above the city) supports the physical sense, not contempt.

forcedChoices.choice: Matthew and Andrew address Jesus with tú
forcedChoices.reason: Disciples speak to one person; the packet asks for tú.
